fixer.summary: A scene's Difficult Terrain (game.scene.difficult) now applies to every mode that spends walking Speed (walk and crawl), not just mode 'walk'. Crawling through rubble therefore costs 3 ft per foot (R-42 Reading A). Climb, swim and fly are unchanged. The fix also makes T-98's red test pass (strict xpass).

review.summary: The fix solves the ticket. The scene's Difficult Terrain check now asks whether the move spends walking Speed (`spec.speed == "walk"`) instead of checking for the literal mode name `"walk"`. Crawl is a walking-Speed mode in `MOVE_MODES`, so crawling through a Difficult Terrain scene now pays 5 + 5 for crawling + 5 for Difficult Terrain, which is 3 ft per foot as R-42 Reading A rules. Asking the existing `MoveMode` data replaces a check on a mode string, so the rule lives in the data and no second mechanism is added. Other modes behave as before. T-98 has the same cause, so its strict xfail had to come off with this fix; removing only the xfail markers is fine and is not scope creep. The new unit test checks real behaviour: a crawl through the scene costs 15, a walk after it costs 10, and the creature ends where it should. The `SRD[...]` comment cites the right clauses and R-42. No hard-coding, layering problems or meaningless tests.
